q: What is the youngest age at which you can get a North Carolina Level 1 Limited Learner Permit?
exp: Level 1 is open to teens from 15 to 17 who have passed driver education.
src: G.S. 20-11; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Graduated Licensing

q: Before testing for a Level 1 permit, a teen must pass a driver education course with at least:
a: 24 hours in the classroom and 6 hours behind the wheel
b: 30 hours in the classroom and 10 hours behind the wheel
c: 30 hours in the classroom and 6 hours behind the wheel
d: 40 hours in the classroom and 8 hours behind the wheel
exp: The approved course is 30 classroom hours plus 6 behind-the-wheel hours.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Graduated Licensing; NCDMV Level 1 page

q: What score do you need to pass the North Carolina knowledge test on traffic laws?
exp: State rule sets the passing score for the knowledge test at 80 percent.
src: 19A NCAC 03B .0201

q: On the separate North Carolina road sign test, how many signs must a Class C applicant identify correctly?
exp: Class C applicants are shown 12 signs and must identify at least 9.
src: 19A NCAC 03B .0201

q: How long must you hold a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit before you can apply for a Level 2 license?
exp: The holding period is nine months, along with a clean record and the driving log.
src: G.S. 20-11(d)(1); NCDMV Level 2 page

q: What does your Level 1 driving log need to show before you apply for Level 2?
a: At least 50 hours, with at least 10 at night
b: At least 60 hours, with at least 6 at night
c: At least 60 hours, with at least 10 at night
d: At least 40 hours, with at least 15 at night
exp: The log must show 60 supervised hours, and 10 of them must be at night.

q: A Level 2 Limited Provisional License lets you drive without a supervisor during which hours?
exp: Unsupervised Level 2 driving is limited to 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., plus trips straight to or from work or volunteer emergency service.

q: Driving alone on a Level 2 license, how many passengers under 21 who are not in your household may ride with you (not counting students going to or from school)?
exp: The limit is one non-household passenger under 21; one more is allowed only if that student is being driven straight to or from school.
src: G.S. 20-11(e)(4); NCDMV Level 2 page

q: A supervising driver for a Level 1 permit holder must have held a driver's license for at least:
exp: The supervisor must be licensed and have been licensed for at least five years.

q: Which statement about phones is true for a North Carolina driver under 18?
a: Hands-free calls to anyone are allowed, but texting is not
b: Handheld calls are allowed on roads posted under 45 mph
c: None while moving, except calls to parents, a spouse or emergency help
d: Texting is allowed if the supervising adult says it is okay
exp: Drivers under 18 may not use a phone while the car is in motion, hands-free or not, except for those calls.

q: During the first six months on a Level 1 permit, when may you drive?
a: At any hour, with your supervising driver
b: Only from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., alone
d: Only from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., with your supervising driver
exp: For six months the permit allows supervised driving from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.; after that, supervised driving at any hour.

q: Who may sit in the front seat while you drive on a Level 1 permit?
d: Your supervisor and one other adult
exp: No one except the driver and the supervising driver may be in the front seat.
src: G.S. 20-11(k); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1

q: Who may serve as the supervising driver for a North Carolina Level 1 permit holder?
b: A parent, grandparent, guardian or responsible adult the parent approves
d: Only a parent or legal guardian
exp: The supervisor must be a parent, grandparent, guardian or an approved responsible adult, licensed at least five years.

q: How many hours of driving in a single week can count toward the Level 1 driving log?
exp: No more than 10 hours per week may be counted toward the 60 hour total.

q: How long must you hold a Level 2 license before moving up to a Level 3 Full Provisional License?
exp: Level 3 requires at least six months on the Level 2 license.

q: What is the earliest age at which a teen can hold a Level 3 Full Provisional License?
exp: Level 2 starts no earlier than 16, and it must be held six months.

q: To move up from Level 1 to Level 2, you must have had no moving violation, seat belt infraction or phone violation in the past:
exp: Both Level 2 and Level 3 require a clean six months before you apply.

q: What happens if a teen's driving log is found to be falsified?
a: The teen pays a $25 fine and keeps the log
b: The permit is cancelled for 30 days
c: The teen must start a new log and wait six months
d: The teen must retake driver education
exp: A falsified log means a new log and a six month wait before eligibility.

q: If you fail the North Carolina knowledge test or road test, when may you try again?
exp: NCDMV lets Class C applicants retake a failed knowledge or road test in seven calendar days.
src: NCDMV Driver License Tests page

q: What visual acuity do you need for a North Carolina license with no vision restriction?
exp: Acuity of 20/40 or better gives an unrestricted license; below that, a lens restriction applies.
src: 19A NCAC 03B .0201

q: Your license says you must wear corrective lenses, and you drive without them. The law treats this the same as:
exp: Driving without required lenses carries the same penalty as driving with no license.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Vision

q: What does a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit cost?
exp: The Level 1 permit fee is $25.50, the same as the Level 2 license.
src: NCDMV fee schedule; NCDMV Level 1 page

q: How is the fee for a regular Class C license figured in North Carolina?
d: $6.50 for each year the license is valid
exp: The Class C fee is $6.50 per year of the license term.
src: NCDMV fee schedule; G.S. 20-7

q: How much extra does a North Carolina REAL ID cost?
exp: Fees for a REAL ID are the same as for a standard card.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, REAL ID

q: How can you tell a North Carolina REAL ID from a standard card?
a: The REAL ID has a red bar
b: The REAL ID has a star
c: The standard card has a star
d: The REAL ID is printed vertically
exp: Every REAL ID carries a star; a standard card says Not for Federal Identification.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, REAL ID

q: A teen tests for a Level 1 permit at an NCDMV office. Who must be there?
a: No one; the teen may come alone
c: A parent or guardian, or someone with their written consent
d: Any adult with a valid license
exp: A parent or guardian must be present, or another adult must bring written consent from one.
src: NCDMV Level 1 page

q: On a Level 2 license, which trip may you make alone after 9 p.m.?
a: Driving home from a friend's house
c: Driving home from a school dance
d: Driving straight home from your job
exp: The only exceptions are going straight to or from work, or to or from volunteer fire, rescue or EMS duty.

q: Where may a North Carolina teen take the road test for a Level 2 license?
a: At an NCDMV office or a certified commercial driving school
c: At any high school parking lot
d: Online, with a video of the drive
exp: The road test may be given by NCDMV or by a driving school the Division has certified.
src: G.S. 20-11(d)(3); NCDMV Level 2 page

q: Which proof of insurance does NCDMV accept when you apply for a license?
d: A verbal statement from your parent
exp: Proof of liability insurance must be printed; images on a mobile device are refused.
src: NCDMV Level 2 page; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Liability Insurance

q: A new resident of North Carolina must get a North Carolina license within how many days?
exp: New residents have 60 days after setting up residence to get a North Carolina license.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Moving to North Carolina

q: An adult moves to North Carolina with a valid license from another state. Which tests does NCDMV give?
a: The knowledge test and the road test
c: Every test, including the road test
d: The road sign test and the vision test
exp: With a valid out-of-state license, the sign and vision tests are required; the knowledge and road tests are usually waived.
src: 19A NCAC 03B .0201(b)(4); NCDMV new residents page

q: An adult who now lives in North Carolina holds only a license from another country. What must they do to get a North Carolina license?
a: Pass the knowledge, sign, vision and road tests
c: Take only the sign and vision tests
d: Show an International Driving Permit instead of testing
exp: A foreign license is not an out-of-state license, so the applicant takes the full examination.
src: 19A NCAC 03B .0201(b)(1); NCDMV new residents page

q: What is the fine for a driver under 18 who uses a phone while driving in North Carolina?
exp: The under 18 phone ban carries a $25 fine with no points or court costs.

q: A provisional licensee (under 18) is convicted of driving after drinking any alcohol. How long is the license revoked?
exp: Any alcohol or drugs while driving under 18 brings a one-year revocation.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, The Provisional Licensee

q: A driver under 18 gets a second moving violation within 12 months. NCDMV may suspend the license for up to:
exp: Second violation: up to 30 days; third: up to 90 days; fourth: up to six months.

q: When does a Level 1 permit or a Level 2 license expire?
b: One year after it is issued
exp: Both expire on the 18th birthday.

q: Which tests does a teen take at the NCDMV office to get a Level 1 permit?
a: Written, sign, vision and road tests
exp: The road test comes later, when you apply for Level 2.
src: NCDMV Level 1 page

q: A regular North Carolina license issued to someone between 18 and 65 is valid for:
exp: Licenses last eight years for ages 18 to 65 and five years from age 66.
src: NCDMV new drivers page; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1

q: Which school document do North Carolina teens no longer need for a permit or license?
b: Proof of a Social Security number
c: Proof of a North Carolina address
exp: S.L. 2026-46 eliminated the Driving Eligibility Certificate; the Driver Education Certificate is still required.
src: S.L. 2026-46, s. 9; NCDMV Level 1 page

q: An adult 18 or older drives on a North Carolina learner permit. Who must be in the car?
a: A person licensed to drive that vehicle, seated beside the driver
b: A licensed driver 25 or older, in any seat
d: No one; adults may drive alone on a permit
exp: The permit holder must be accompanied by a person licensed for that vehicle and seated beside them.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Learner Permit

q: What is the fine for speeding in a North Carolina school zone?
exp: Speeding in a school zone is an infraction with a $250 fine, plus 3 license points.

q: In a North Carolina work zone where signs post the penalty, speeding adds what on top of the normal fine?
exp: A $250 work zone penalty is added when signs at the start of the zone state it.

q: How many points go on a North Carolina license for speeding in a school zone?
exp: Speeding over the posted school zone limit carries 3 points.

q: What is the lowest speed limit North Carolina allows to be set in a school zone?
exp: A school zone limit may not be set below 20 mph.

q: Failing to yield in a North Carolina work zone causes serious injury. What is the penalty?
c: A $500 fine and a 90-day license revocation
d: A warning and driver improvement clinic
exp: Failure to yield that causes serious bodily injury in a work zone brings a $500 fine and 90-day revocation.
src: G.S. 20-160.1; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 3

q: On the sign test you see a red, eight-sided sign. What does it mean?
exp: The octagon is used only for stop signs.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A triangle pointing down, with a red border and white center, tells you to:
a: Slow down and give the right of way
exp: The downward triangle is the yield sign; stop only if traffic requires it.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A fluorescent yellow-green five-sided sign shaped like a house warns of:
exp: The pentagon is reserved for school signs.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow, sideways triangle on the left side of the road marks:
a: A sharp curve to the left
b: A road entering from the left
c: The start of a no-passing zone
d: The end of a divided highway
exp: The pennant points to where the no-passing zone begins.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR means:
exp: The circle is the railroad advance warning sign; slow down, look and listen.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A white X-shaped sign reading RAILROAD CROSSING stands at the tracks. Treat it like:
exp: At a crossbuck, slow down and yield to any train; stop if one is coming.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A red circle with a white horizontal bar across it means:
b: Do not enter from this side
exp: The Do Not Enter sign faces traffic at the wrong end of ramps and one-way streets.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: You pass a red rectangular sign reading WRONG WAY. What does it tell you?
a: The road curves the wrong way for trucks
exp: Pull over safely and turn around when no traffic is coming.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: What color are signs that warn of road construction or maintenance?
exp: Black on orange is reserved for work zones; yellow is the general warning color.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Work Zones

q: A diamond-shaped sign is usually used for:
a: A warning about the road ahead
exp: Diamonds are warning signs, normally black on yellow.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: Blue guide signs point to:
b: Services such as gas, food and hospitals
exp: Blue is the color for driver services.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A brown guide sign points to:
exp: Brown signs mark recreation and cultural sites.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sec. 2A.06, Table 2A-2

q: A fluorescent pink sign warns of:
d: A crash or incident scene ahead
exp: Fluorescent pink is used for temporary incident management.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sec. 2A.06, Table 2A-2; Sec. 6H.01

q: A yellow diamond showing a car with wavy marks behind it means:
a: The road is slippery when wet
exp: Slow down in rain and avoid hard braking or sharp steering.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond showing one lane joining another from the side warns that:
b: Traffic will enter your lane ahead
exp: The merge sign means make room for vehicles merging in.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond showing two arrows, one pointing up and one down, means:
exp: You are leaving a one-way or divided road; traffic will come toward you.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow sign showing the median of a divided road ending warns that:
b: The road ends at a T
d: Oncoming traffic will soon be beside you with no divider
exp: Divided Highway Ends means you will share an undivided road with oncoming traffic.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: An orange diamond showing a person holding a paddle means:
a: A flagger is ahead; be ready to stop
b: A school crossing guard is ahead
exp: Flaggers use a STOP/SLOW paddle to control traffic in work zones.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Work Zones

q: A square yellow plaque reading 25 MPH under a curve sign shows:
a: The legal speed limit for the road
b: The advised safe speed for the curve
c: The minimum speed for the curve
exp: Advisory speeds are advice for good conditions; the legal limit is on the white sign.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: Compared with a curve sign, a turn sign (an arrow bent at a right angle) warns of:
b: A road entering from the side
c: A sharper bend that needs a slower speed
exp: A turn is sharper than a curve, so slow down more.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond with a symbol shaped like the letter Y means:
exp: A Y intersection splits the road; pick your branch early.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond showing a straight arrow with a short line leaving one side warns of:
a: A side road entering from that side
b: A lane ending on that side
exp: Watch for vehicles entering from the side road.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond with three curved arrows in a circle warns of:
exp: The circular intersection sign means a roundabout is ahead.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond sign with the words ONE LANE BRIDGE means:
a: The bridge is closed to trucks and buses
b: Trucks must use the right lane on the bridge
c: One vehicle at a time; yield to a car already on it
d: Each direction has its own lane on the bridge
exp: Room for one vehicle: wait for oncoming traffic on the bridge to clear.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond sign with the words LOW SHOULDER warns that:
a: Parking is allowed on the shoulder
b: The shoulder is soft sand or mud
c: The road narrows to one lane
d: The shoulder is lower than the road
exp: A wheel that drops off the edge can pull the car; steer back on gently.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond sign with the words NO OUTLET means:
a: The road ahead has no other way out
b: The road ends at a wall or barrier
c: No trucks or buses are allowed
exp: No Outlet means you will have to come back the way you went in.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A red eight-sided stop sign has a white plaque below it reading EXCEPT RIGHT TURN. What does it mean?
a: Drivers turning right must stop; others may go
b: Right turns need not stop; all others must
c: Right turns are not allowed at this stop
d: Right turns are allowed on a red light
exp: The plaque exempts right-turning drivers from the stop.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow EXIT ONLY panel above your lane on a freeway means:
a: The exit ahead is closed today
b: You may exit or continue in this lane
c: This lane leaves the freeway; you must exit
d: Trucks must exit; cars may continue
exp: Move out of an Exit Only lane early if you are not exiting.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A white sign reading CENTER LANE LEFT TURN ONLY means the center lane may be used:
b: As a travel lane at rush hour
d: Only for left turns, from both directions
exp: A shared center turn lane is never a passing lane.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond showing a tipping truck on a curved arrow warns:
a: Trucks have rolled over on this curve; slow down
b: Trucks must use a lower gear
exp: The Truck Rollover sign marks a curve that is dangerous at speed.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A yellow diamond showing a traffic light with red, yellow and green lights warns of:
b: A traffic signal ahead, possibly hidden
c: A signal ahead that is not working
d: A flashing school zone light ahead
exp: Start slowing; the signal is around a curve or over a hill.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A white sign shows a vertical road crossing a wide divided road. It tells you that:
b: You may turn left directly across both roadways
c: You will cross two separate roadways; treat each as its own street
exp: At a divided highway crossing, cross the first roadway, then the second.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: A plaque under a yield sign reads TO ONCOMING TRAFFIC. What must you do?
a: Yield only to traffic behind you
d: Let vehicles coming toward you go first
exp: This plaque often stands at a one-lane bridge or narrow road.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signs; MUTCD 11th ed.

q: On North Carolina roads, the state route marker is shaped like:
exp: NC route markers are diamond-shaped; U.S. routes use a shield.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Guide Signs

q: At a steady red light in North Carolina, when may you turn right?
a: Without stopping, if no cars are coming
c: Never; right on red is illegal
d: After a complete stop, unless a sign forbids it
exp: Stop fully, then yield to traffic and pedestrians before turning right on red.

q: May you turn left on a red light in North Carolina from a one-way street onto another one-way street?
a: No, North Carolina allows right on red only
b: Yes, after a full stop and yielding
c: Yes, if no traffic is coming either way
d: Yes, from the far left lane after stopping
exp: State law authorizes a turn on steady red only to the right.

q: What does a steady red arrow mean in North Carolina?
b: Stop; no turn is allowed in that direction
c: Turn right after a full stop
exp: A solid red arrow means stop, with no turns that way.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Flashing Yellow Arrow Signal Heads

q: Turning right on red, a North Carolina driver fails to yield to a pedestrian starting to cross. The court may impose a penalty of:
exp: The pedestrian yield penalty is not less than $100 and not more than $500.

q: On a divided highway with a median, a school bus stops with red lights flashing. Who must stop?
d: No one; the median protects children
exp: On a divided highway with a median, traffic going the other way may proceed with care.
src: G.S. 20-217(c); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, School Buses

q: On a four-lane road with no median, a school bus stops to load children. Who must stop?
c: Only traffic in the lane next to the bus
exp: Without a median, all four lanes stop.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, School Buses

q: A school bus stops on a road of four or more lanes with a center turn lane. Who must stop?
b: Only vehicles in the center lane
d: No one, if the bus is on the shoulder
exp: With four or more lanes and a center turning lane, only traffic behind the bus stops.
src: G.S. 20-217(c); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4

q: Passing a stopped school bus in North Carolina adds how many points to your license?
exp: Passing a stopped school bus is a 5 point offense, with a fine of at least $500.

q: A second conviction for passing a stopped school bus within three years brings:
exp: A second misdemeanor violation within three years means a one-year revocation.

q: On a road with two lanes in your direction, you approach a tow truck stopped on the shoulder with flashing lights. What does North Carolina law require?
a: Stop behind the tow truck until it leaves
b: Move into the lane not next to it, if safe
c: Stay in your lane and keep your speed
d: Use the shoulder to pass on the right
exp: Move over when you safely can; if not, slow down and be ready to stop.

q: What is the fine for violating North Carolina's Move Over law?
exp: A Move Over violation is an infraction with a $250 fine.

q: The Move Over law applies to an emergency or service vehicle stopped within how many feet of the road with its lights on?
exp: The law covers vehicles parked or standing within 12 feet of the roadway.

q: A fire truck passes you on the way to a fire inside city limits. How close may you follow it?
d: As close as you like if you signal
exp: Inside a city or town, stay at least one block back; outside, 400 feet.

q: Police are working a crash on the shoulder. How close may you park to their vehicles?
exp: Do not park within 100 feet of emergency vehicles at a crash scene.

q: Failing to stop for a siren in North Carolina adds how many points to your license?
exp: Failure to stop for a siren is a 3 point offense.

q: In North Carolina, how far before a turn must you signal on a road posted under 45 mph?
exp: Signal continuously for at least the last 100 feet before you stop or turn.

q: Where the speed limit is 45 mph or more, North Carolina requires a turn signal for at least the last:
exp: At 45 mph or higher, signal for at least 200 feet before turning.

q: You miss your exit on a North Carolina Interstate. What should you do?
a: Make a U-turn through the median
c: Stop and wait for a gap
d: Go on to the next exit
exp: U-turns on controlled-access highways are illegal except through openings built for them.
src: G.S. 20-140.3; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Interstate Highways

q: When you and an oncoming driver both have green arrows, you to make a U-turn and they to turn right, who yields?
d: No one; both arrows protect you
exp: U-turning traffic yields to opposing right-turning traffic when both have green arrows.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic Signals

q: In a single-lane North Carolina roundabout, how far around do you go to make a U-turn?
b: All the way around the circle
exp: A full circle is a U-turn; three quarters is a left turn.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Roundabouts

q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit inside North Carolina cities and towns?
exp: The default limit in municipal limits is 35 mph.

q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit outside North Carolina cities and towns?
exp: The default outside municipal limits is 55 mph.

q: What is the highest speed limit North Carolina may post on an Interstate?
exp: Interstate limits may be raised to no more than 70 mph.
src: G.S. 20-141(d); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4

q: How many points does North Carolina assign for speeding at more than 55 mph?
exp: Speeding in excess of 55 mph carries 3 points; most other moving violations carry 2.

q: In North Carolina, driving more than 15 mph over the limit, or faster than 80 mph, is:
exp: Both are Class 3 misdemeanors.

q: A driver going faster than 55 mph is convicted of going more than 15 mph over the limit. The license is taken for at least:
exp: That conviction brings a revocation of at least 30 days.
src: G.S. 20-16.1(a); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 3, Suspensions

q: Under a new North Carolina law, what is the speed limit on an unpaved road or a road with no center line?
exp: S.L. 2026-46 sets 25 mph on unpaved roads and roads without a center line.
src: S.L. 2026-46, s. 17 (amends G.S. 20-141(b), effective December 1, 2026)

q: What following distance does the North Carolina Driver Handbook teach for good conditions?
exp: The handbook uses the two-second rule and asks for more space in bad conditions.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Following

q: On wet pavement, the North Carolina Driver Handbook says to leave at least:
exp: Stopping takes two to 10 times as far on slippery roads, so double your gap.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Rain

q: How many points does following too closely add to a North Carolina license?
exp: Following too closely is a 4 point offense.

q: On the I-77 Express Lanes near Charlotte, which vehicles ride free?
d: Vehicles carrying three or more people, after declaring it
exp: HOV3+ vehicles ride free when the driver declares it through NC Quick Pass.
src: FHWA, I-77 Express Lanes project profile

q: The former HOV lanes on I-77 north of Charlotte are now:
exp: The carpool lanes were converted to express toll lanes with electronic tolling.
src: FHWA, I-77 Express Lanes project profile

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in North Carolina?
exp: Parking within 15 feet of a hydrant or fire station entrance is banned.

q: Where there is a curb, how far must you park from the curb line of an intersecting street in North Carolina?
exp: Stay 25 feet from the curb line; 15 feet from the property lines if there is no curb.

q: You must stop on a highway shoulder. From how far must approaching drivers be able to see your car in both directions?
exp: Shoulder parking is legal only where drivers can see the car from 200 feet both ways.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Parking

q: Outside city limits, how close to a fire or fire truck may you park?
exp: Inside city limits the distance is one block; outside, 400 feet.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Parking; G.S. 20-157(c)

q: When you pass any vehicle, a bicycle included, North Carolina law requires you to pass at least how far to its left?
exp: The passing driver must clear the vehicle by at least two feet; changing lanes is safest.
src: G.S. 20-149(a); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Passing

q: When may you pass a bicycle in a North Carolina no-passing zone?
a: If it is going under 15 mph and you leave 3 feet
b: If the cyclist waves you on and you leave 2 feet
c: If it is not turning left and you leave 4 feet or change lanes
d: If it is going under 10 mph and you stay within the speed limit
exp: The exception also requires the bicycle or moped to be traveling in your direction.

q: A driver turns without signaling and forces a cyclist out of the lane. The minimum fine is:
exp: Forcing a bicycle or motorcycle rider to change lanes or leave the road costs at least $200.

q: A crash in North Carolina must be reported to police at once if anyone is hurt or property damage appears to reach at least:
exp: A reportable crash involves death, injury, or total property damage of $1,000 or more.
src: G.S. 20-4.01(33b); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Crashes

q: After a crash on a North Carolina highway with no injuries, what should you do with a car that can still be driven?
a: Leave it exactly where it stopped
b: Drive home and call police later
c: Stay in the car with the engine running
d: Move it out of the travel lane onto the shoulder
exp: If no one is hurt and the car runs safely, clear the travel lanes.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Crashes

q: Failing to report a crash that the law requires you to report adds how many points?
exp: Failure to report a reportable crash is a 3 point offense.

q: In North Carolina, you must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
exp: Beams must not glare into the eyes of anyone within 500 feet ahead.

q: When following another vehicle, North Carolina requires low beams within:
exp: Dim when following at less than 200 feet, unless you are passing.

q: When does North Carolina require your headlights to be on during the day?
a: Whenever you drive on an Interstate
b: In school zones during posted hours
c: When the sky is cloudy or overcast
d: When wipers run because of the weather
exp: Headlights must be on whenever wipers run because of the weather, except intermittent use in a light mist.

q: North Carolina requires headlights whenever you cannot clearly see a person on the road how far ahead?
exp: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility of a person drops below 400 feet.

q: Which lights does the North Carolina Driver Handbook tell you to use in fog?
exp: High beams reflect off fog; use low beams and slow down.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, Fog

q: Police signal you to stop, but there is no safe place to pull over. What does the North Carolina Driver Handbook advise?
a: Stop in the travel lane at once
b: Speed up to find an exit quickly
c: Turn on your flashers and slow by about 10 mph until you reach a safe spot
d: Ignore the officer until you get home
exp: Flashers and a slower speed show the officer you know they are there.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, When Stopped By Law Enforcement

q: An unmarked car signals you to stop and you are unsure it is really police. The North Carolina Driver Handbook says you may:
c: Get out and walk to the car
d: Call 911 before pulling over to confirm
exp: Give 911 your name and location so they can confirm the stop.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, When Stopped By Law Enforcement

q: During a traffic stop in North Carolina, what are you required by state law to show the officer?
a: Your driver's license and the vehicle registration
exp: State law requires you to identify yourself and give your license and registration.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4, When Stopped By Law Enforcement

q: For a North Carolina driver under 21, how much alcohol in the body is illegal while driving?
exp: Drivers under 21 may not drive with any alcohol or controlled substance in the body.

q: What is the illegal BAC for a North Carolina driver of a commercial motor vehicle?
exp: Commercial drivers are impaired per se at 0.04.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 2, Driving While Impaired

q: At what BAC is a North Carolina driver 21 or older guilty of impaired driving per se?
exp: At 0.08 or more, the driver is impaired by law, whatever their driving looks like.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 2, Driving While Impaired

q: Besides an immediate 30-day revocation, what does refusing a chemical test bring in North Carolina?
d: Nothing, if you are later found not guilty
exp: Refusal brings an immediate revocation of at least 30 days and a 12-month DMV revocation.
src: G.S. 20-16.2; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 2

q: Before a chemical test, you ask for a lawyer. How long can the test be delayed for the lawyer or a witness to arrive?
exp: Testing may not be delayed more than 30 minutes from when you are told your rights.

q: What happens to your license on a first impaired driving conviction in North Carolina?
a: It is revoked for one year
exp: A first DWI conviction carries a mandatory one-year revocation.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 2, Alcohol and the Young Driver

q: What is the maximum fine for Level Five, the lowest level of impaired driving punishment in North Carolina?
exp: Level Five carries 24 hours to 60 days in jail and a fine of up to $200.

q: A North Carolina driver is convicted of impaired driving with a BAC of 0.15 or more. What must be installed?
exp: A conviction at 0.15 or higher requires an ignition interlock.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 2, Blood Alcohol Concentration Restrictions

q: Under North Carolina's open container law, where may an open container of alcohol not be kept while on the road?
d: Anywhere in the passenger area, including the glove box
exp: The passenger area includes the glove compartment; the trunk is excluded.

q: A 19-year-old tries to buy beer with a fake ID in North Carolina. What happens to the driver's license?
a: It is revoked for one year
c: Nothing, since no car was involved
exp: Attempting to buy alcohol under 21, or using a fake ID to get it, brings a one-year revocation.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 2, Alcohol and the Young Driver

q: A 22-year-old gives beer to an 18-year-old friend. What license penalty does North Carolina law set?
a: None; only the minor is punished
exp: Giving an alcoholic beverage to anyone under 21 also brings a one-year revocation.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 2, Alcohol and the Young Driver

q: Which drivers does North Carolina's ban on texting and reading email while driving cover?
exp: Typing or reading texts and email while driving is banned for every driver; the fine is $100.

q: What is the fine for an adult texting while driving in North Carolina?
exp: Texting while driving is an infraction with a $100 fine and no license points.

q: Who in a moving car must wear a seat belt under North Carolina law?
exp: Every occupant must be belted whenever the car moves.

q: What is the penalty for an unbelted rear seat adult passenger in North Carolina?
b: A $10 penalty with no court costs
exp: Rear seat violations cost $10 and cannot by themselves justify a traffic stop.

q: What is the fine for an unbelted driver or front seat passenger in North Carolina?
exp: Front seat violations are infractions with a $25.50 penalty plus court costs, and no points.

q: A North Carolina child under 8 who weighs less than 80 pounds must ride in:
a: A lap and shoulder belt alone
b: An adult's lap in the back seat
c: The front seat with a booster
d: A child seat suited to its weight
exp: Children under 8 and under 80 pounds need a weight-appropriate child restraint system.

q: If the car has a front passenger airbag and a back seat, which child must ride in the back?
a: A child under 5 weighing under 40 pounds
c: A child under 12 weighing under 100 pounds
exp: Unless the seat is designed for use with airbags, that child rides in the rear seat.

q: How many license points does a child restraint violation carry in North Carolina?
exp: The penalty is up to $25 and 2 driver license points.

q: Children under what age may not ride in the open bed of a pickup truck in North Carolina, with few exceptions?
exp: Riding in an open bed is banned for children under 16 unless an exception applies.
src: G.S. 20-135.2B; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 4

q: What is North Carolina's minimum liability insurance for injury to one person?
exp: The minimums are $50,000 per person, $100,000 per crash for injuries and $50,000 for property damage.

q: When can you get your North Carolina vehicle inspection before your registration renews?
c: Any time in the past two years
exp: Annual inspections may be done up to 90 days before the registration expires.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 7, Vehicle Emissions and Safety Inspection

q: After you move within North Carolina, how long do you have to update your license address?
exp: Address and name changes must be reported within 60 days.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Address Changes

q: At how many points may North Carolina send you to a driver improvement clinic?
exp: At 7 points you may be assigned a clinic; finishing it removes 3 points.
src: G.S. 20-16(c); NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 3, Points

q: Your North Carolina license can be suspended if you build up how many points within three years?
exp: Twelve points in three years can bring a suspension; eight after a reinstatement.

q: How long can a first point-system suspension in North Carolina last?
exp: The first point suspension is up to 60 days, the second six months, later ones one year.

q: Which maneuver will you be asked to perform on the North Carolina road test?
exp: The road test includes a three-point turnabout, a quick stop and backing.
src: 19A NCAC 03B .0201; NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1

q: On the North Carolina road test, what is a quick stop?
b: Stopping only with the parking brake
c: Stopping as fast as you safely can when told to
exp: The examiner tells you when to make it; stay in control.
src: NC Driver Handbook (rev. May 2025), Ch. 1, Skills Observed

q: Who must be present when a teen takes the Level 2 road test at an NCDMV office?
exp: A parent or guardian must be present for the road test, or give written consent.
src: NCDMV Level 2 page

q: What happens before the North Carolina road test begins?
a: A pre-trip check that your car is safe
b: A second vision test at the counter
c: A parking drill between two cones
d: A short quiz of 10 road law questions
exp: A car that fails the pre-trip inspection cannot be used for the test.
src: NCDMV Level 2 page

q: You fail the North Carolina road test. When may you take it again?
exp: The retest wait for a regular Class C road test is seven calendar days.
src: NCDMV Driver License Tests page
